root_cause: The middleware runner read the framework-internal `x-middleware-subrequest` header (meant to stop middleware recursion) straight from the incoming request and skipped middleware when it matched, and the header was not stripped from external requests, so an outside request could claim to be an internal subrequest.
notes: 52a078da is the commit in tag v15.2.3 (vulnerable tag v15.2.2); the same change landed on canary as 9704c8e9fcc58236349ed787903831579440a879. The fix adds a per-process random `x-middleware-subrequest-id` and drops `x-middleware-subrequest` when the id does not match (router-server.ts, server-ipc/utils.ts, sandbox/context.ts). Also fixed in 14.2.25, 13.5.9 and 12.3.5; those backports were not traced to commits.

root_cause: The authentication exemption could be claimed by a request to `/_layouts/15/ToolPane.aspx` whose Referer named the sign-out page (CVE-2025-53771), and ToolPane.aspx then deserialized request-supplied data into objects (CVE-2025-53770); machineKey values stolen from servers additionally let attacker-signed ViewState pass validation and be deserialized.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affects on-premises SharePoint Server 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition; SharePoint Online is not affected. CVE-2025-53770 is described as a bypass of the July 2025 fix for CVE-2025-49704. The deserializing class and method are not named in the sources read.

root_cause: The S3-compatible AWS4-HMAC authorization path of the HTTP(S) server looked up the user named in the header with a `lookup_user_pass` flag that defaulted to true, so the user was loaded without a password check, and the handling had a race condition that let the resulting session be used.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affected 10.0.0 through 10.8.3 and 11.0.0 through 11.3.0; fixed in 10.8.4 and 11.3.1. Instances behind a CrushFTP DMZ proxy instance are not affected (CVE record).

root_cause: When no DMZ proxy instance was deployed in front of the server, AS2 message validation (including the Message Integrity Check) was not enforced on the HTTPS path, so crafted requests were treated as coming from a trusted source and reached admin functions.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affected: all 10.x below 10.8.5 and 11.x below 11.3.4_23; deployments with a DMZ CrushFTP instance in front are not affected (vendor page). The vendor code change is not public.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The `POST /api/v1/validate/code` route had no current-user dependency, so unauthenticated request bodies reached `validate_code`, which imports modules and runs `exec` on the submitted function definitions.
notes: Fix commit parent is e1ee081d3223bd2150425ddb9487b5e9f4ccff26. Last affected tag 1.2.0; first fixed tag 1.3.0 (langflow-base 0.3.0). The patch only adds the `CurrentActiveUser` dependency to the route; the exec path is unchanged. Hand the reviewer src/backend/base/langflow/utils/validate.py together with the audit scope so the exec sink is visible.

root_cause: The unauthenticated public-flow endpoint `build_public_tmp` accepted an optional `data` body and passed it to `start_flow_build`, which then built the graph from caller-supplied nodes instead of the stored flow, so caller-supplied component code reached `exec`.
notes: Fix commit parent is 1fdbbfaab16f0df07a70b49563805a69210c5059; tag 1.8.1 is vulnerable. Sources conflict on the first fixed release: the GHSA lists 1.8.2 as affected and 1.9.0 as patched, but tag 1.8.2 already contains the fix commit; use the commit refs above. The exec sink is `prepare_global_scope` in src/lfx/src/lfx/custom/validate.py (outside the audit scope).

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
root_cause: For the `/api/v2/featureusage` API, request validation (`DeviceFeatureUsageReportQueryRequestValidator`) ran before Spring Security authentication, and the validator built its error message from the user-supplied `format` value through message interpolation that evaluates EL expressions.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in 11.12.0.5, 12.3.0.2, 12.4.0.2 and 12.5.0.1 (on-prem EPMM only). Class and endpoint names come from public analyses of decompiled code.

root_cause: Apache RewriteMap handed unauthenticated request URLs to Bash helper scripts (such as `map-appstore-url`), which parsed URL parameters into shell variables and compared them in a `[[ ... -gt ... ]]` arithmetic context, where Bash evaluates variable references and array subscripts, including command substitution.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affects the In-House Application Distribution and Android File Transfer Configuration features of on-prem EPMM. Per watchTowr, the fix replaced the Bash RewriteMap scripts with Java classes. The Ivanti security advisory itself was not located; the Ivanti analysis-guidance page is linked instead.

root_cause: The web server copied the `X-Forwarded-For` header into a fixed-size stack buffer without bounding the copy, a stack overflow that the vendor first treated as a non-security bug because the accepted characters were limited to digits and dots.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in Connect Secure 22.7R2.6 (released February 2025 as a product bug fix), Policy Secure 22.7R1.4 and ZTA Gateways 22.8R2.2; Pulse Connect Secure 9.x is end of life and affected.

component: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
root_cause: When the `login` form field was missing or empty in a request to the authentication handler, the value was left uninitialized and was still echoed into the response, so stack memory (including session tokens) was disclosed.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in 14.1-43.56 and 13.1-58.32 and later (plus FIPS/NDcPP builds listed in CTX693420). Reachable when the appliance is configured as a Gateway or AAA virtual server; the endpoint named in analyses is /p/u/doAuthentication.do.

root_cause: The Node.js websocket CLI module accepted a request-supplied `local_access_token` in place of a session check and then accepted an unverified login context (user and profile) sent over its local CLI bridge, so the caller's own claim became a super_admin session (CVE-2024-55591); crafted CSF proxy requests bypassed authentication the same way (CVE-2025-24472).
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Both CVEs are in FG-IR-24-535; see it for affected and fixed versions. The record wording says the modules trusted a serial number the request reported about itself; the sources read describe an unvalidated access-token parameter plus an unverified self-asserted user/profile (and a race) for CVE-2024-55591, and give no technical detail for the CSF proxy path of CVE-2025-24472.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: A relative path inside an API URL resolved to the legacy `fwbcgi` CGI handler outside the API's authentication, and that handler's `cgi_auth()` took the user and profile to act as from a Base64 JSON `CGIINFO` request header and set the login context without any password check.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affected FortiWeb 8.0.0-8.0.1, 7.6.0-7.6.4, 7.4.0-7.4.9, 7.2.0-7.2.11 and 7.0.0-7.0.11. Function names come from watchTowr's analysis of the firmware.

component: Fortinet FortiCloud SSO login (FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager)
root_cause: The FortiCloud SSO login handler at `/remote/saml/login` did not properly verify the cryptographic signature of the SAML response, so a crafted response was accepted as a valid login.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Exploitable only when FortiCloud SSO login is enabled on the device. FG-IR-25-647 also covers CVE-2025-59719 (FortiWeb).

component: Fortinet FortiCloud SSO login (FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiProxy, FortiWeb)
root_cause: Administrative FortiCloud SSO login accepted a valid SSO identity from any FortiCloud account without checking that it belonged to the account the target device is registered to, so one account's login worked on other accounts' devices.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Requires FortiCloud SSO to be enabled on the device and an attacker-owned FortiCloud account with a registered device. The exact device-side and cloud-side check that was missing is not described in the sources read.

component: Oracle E-Business Suite (Concurrent Processing / BI Publisher Integration)
classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: An unauthenticated request could make the server fetch a URL it chose (SSRF) with CRLF injected into the outgoing request, and a path traversal slipped past the authentication filter to a template endpoint, so an attacker-hosted XSLT was fetched and executed.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affects E-Business Suite 12.2.3 through 12.2.14. The Oracle alert page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; its URL was confirmed through search results.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The Visual Composer development server's `/developmentserver/metadatauploader` endpoint had no authorization check and stored uploaded files where the Java application server would serve and execute them.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Component VCFRAMEWORK 7.50. The vendor fix is SAP Security Note 3594142, which requires an SAP login and is not linked.

root_cause: Connection-protocol messages (number 80 and above, such as channel open and exec requests) were dispatched to `ssh_connection:handle_msg/4` in any state of the server state machine, and no clause checked that user authentication had finished.
notes: Fix spans three commits titled 'ssh: early RCE fix', one per maintenance line, each merged forward: OTP-27 6eef041 (parent = tag OTP-27.3.2, first fixed OTP-27.3.3), OTP-26 b1924d3 (parent = OTP-26.2.5.10, fixed OTP-26.2.5.11), OTP-25 0fcd9c5 (parent = OTP-25.3.2.19, fixed OTP-25.3.2.20). On master the first tag with the fix is OTP-28.0-rc4. The patch adds an early clause that disconnects when a connection message arrives before authentication. For a narrower review, ssh_connection.erl, ssh_connection_handler.erl and ssh_fsm_userauth_server.erl hold the relevant state handling.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: The pre-authentication `deployWebpackage.do` endpoint fetched a package from a caller-chosen host without restricting the target (SSRF), and the service-pack install step extracted the fetched ZIP without confining entry paths, so files landed in the web-served directory.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Only the 11.38 Innovation Release is affected (11.38.0 through 11.38.19); fixed in 11.38.20 and later with the cumulative updates listed in the vendor advisory.

component: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE-PIC
root_cause: An internal API method reachable without authentication (`enableStrongSwanTunnel` in `DescriptionRegistrationListener`, under `/deployment-rpc/`) deserialized the request body and used its content in a command run as root without validating it; the first fix (CVE-2025-20281) was incomplete and CVE-2025-20337 completed it.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Affects ISE and ISE-PIC 3.3 and 3.4. The Cisco advisory also covers CVE-2025-20282 (file upload, 3.4 only), which is not part of this sample. Class and method names come from the ZDI write-up.

component: Cisco ISE cloud deployments (AWS, Azure, OCI)
root_cause: Credentials were generated at cloud deployment time in a way that made them identical across all deployments of the same release on the same cloud platform, so a credential taken from one deployment worked on others.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Only deployments where the Primary Administration Node runs in the cloud are affected; on-premises deployments are not.

root_cause: When decoding a Flight reply, the server resolved client-supplied export names and reference paths with plain property access (`requireModule` returned `moduleExports[metadata[NAME]]`, and model path walks did the same) without an own-property check, so a name could resolve through the prototype chain to built-ins such as the Function constructor.
notes: Main-branch fix 7dc903cd (parent 36df5e8b42a97df4092f9584e4695bf4537853d5). Backports: 19.2 b180cb2b25e60f6d8af5e41673d6983b409fafc3, 19.1 0e2ae74309fd167922ab141556035623b286e798, 19.0 bbed0b0ee64b89353a40d6313037bbc80221bc3d. Tags: vulnerable v19.2.0 / v19.1.1 / v19.0.0, fixed v19.2.1 / v19.1.2 / v19.0.1. The fix is a large refactor that adds hasOwnProperty guards in several places; the advisory does not say which access was the exploited one, so judge both the requireModule lookup and the reply path walks. Frameworks bundling RSC (for example Next.js) shipped their own fixed versions.

classes: Multiple representations of the same fact
root_cause: Signature validation located the Signature and SignedInfo elements with REXML but canonicalized and hashed with Nokogiri, and nothing tied the digested element and the signed SignedInfo to the same parse tree, so the signature could be checked on one tree while assertion data was read from another.
notes: One commit on master fixes both CVEs (PR #750). Tags: vulnerable v1.17.0, fixed v1.18.0. The 1.12.x line was fixed by e76c5b36bac40aedbf1ba7ffaaf495be63328cd9 plus follow-up 48cc5b92e1dde8637a013dfd48cdf8ceadd499b2 (vulnerable v1.12.3, fixed v1.12.4).

root_cause: With SAML SSO and the optional encrypted assertions feature enabled, the SAML response signature was not verified correctly, so a forged response could provision or sign in as a user with site administrator privileges.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in 3.9.15, 3.10.12, 3.11.10 and 3.12.4; all versions before 3.13.0 were affected. CVE-2024-9487 is a follow-up hardening of the same feature.

classes: Whether declared controls actually take effect
root_cause: When matching a method against methods of generic superclasses or generic interfaces, the security annotation scanner resolved an unbounded generic parameter type to null, so the override was not recognized and `@PreAuthorize` and similar annotations declared there were never found or applied.
notes: e5694ac is on the 6.4.x line (parent 9de0aad31ba4a6a359609ef3e6cc3392fe280832) and was merged into 6.5.x by d0f93fa6. The code fix is in tags 6.4.10 and 6.5.4 (the GHSA agrees; vulnerable tags 6.4.9 and 6.5.3), while the spring.io advisory names 6.4.11 and 6.5.5 as fixed; the reason for the difference was not confirmed. The fix falls back to Object for unbounded type parameters. The companion Spring Framework issue CVE-2025-41249 is not part of this sample.

root_cause: The default allow list of image-processing methods (`supported_image_processing_methods`) included three unsafe methods (`apply`, `loader`, `saver`), so a transformation method name taken from user input could pass validation and inject commands through the image processor.
notes: 1ca278a6 is on main; backports: 8-0 2d612735 (fixed v8.0.2.1, vulnerable v8.0.2), 7-2 fb8f3a18 (fixed v7.2.2.2, vulnerable v7.2.2.1), 7-1 1b1adf6e (fixed v7.1.5.2, vulnerable v7.1.5.1). Only the mini_magick processor is affected, and only when applications pass user input as transformation method names. An open PR (https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/56995) claims the Vips path lacks an allow list; that claim is unconfirmed and not part of this sample.

root_cause: The OAuth authorization URL, built from the `authorization_endpoint` that the remote MCP server supplies in its metadata, was passed to the `open` package (the system URL opener) without a scheme allow list or encoding of its parts.
notes: Fix came in two steps. 783bf86 'Sanitizing URLs before invoking open()' (parent 2a0665de6c5a0cec0695effe592aec7a34c5f215 = tag v0.1.14) added sanitizeUrl() in src/lib/utils.ts with an http/https allow list and component encoding, shipped in v0.1.15. 607b226 'Forcibly escape username/pass for basic auth URLs too' (parent = tag v0.1.15), the commit the CVE and GHSA cite, also encodes the username and password; first fixed tag v0.1.16. The advisory calls v0.1.15 affected, but on v0.1.15 only the unencoded username/password part remains, so vulnerable_ref points at v0.1.14 code, where the whole root cause is visible. The SDK code that builds the authorization URL was not read.

root_cause: The Inspector proxy server exposed endpoints that spawn stdio processes from request parameters (`command`, `args`, `env`) with no authentication, accepted any origin through `cors()`, and listened on all interfaces, so any caller that could reach it, including a web page in the local browser, could start commands.
notes: The fix is a merge commit 'Merge commit from fork - Address inspector security vulnerabilities'; its first parent 03edbb01ce06f020314582384fbe3f486510c0d0 is main before the merge. Tags (no v prefix): vulnerable 0.14.0, fixed 0.14.1. The fix adds a random session token checked on every endpoint (opt-out DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH), an Origin allow list (ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and binding to 127.0.0.1 by default (HOST). Every line of the merge diff was not read; the vulnerable server/src/index.ts at 0.14.0 was.

root_cause: Allowed-directory checks used `startsWith(dir)` with no path-separator boundary, so sibling directories sharing a prefix passed (CVE-2025-53110), and when a symlink's resolved target was outside the allowed directories the denial was thrown inside a `try` whose `catch` fell back to checking only the parent directory, so the link was accepted (CVE-2025-53109).
notes: d00c60d 'Address symlink and path prefix issues with allowed directories' (parent b7c48c79ee4096c1d3fdebe0089d81122d6cc051) holds the code change; cc99bda is its merge into main. Repo tags: last before the fix 2025.5.12 (package.json version 0.6.2), first fixed 2025.7.1. On npm the last affected release is 2025.3.28 and the first fixed 2025.7.1; the advisories' '0.6.3' and the CVE record's '<0.6.4' do not match any npm release. The fix adds src/filesystem/path-validation.ts (isPathWithinAllowedDirectories), makes the parent-directory fallback run only for ENOENT, resolves allowed directories with realpath at startup, and makes write_file and applyFileEdits refuse to follow existing symlinks (wx flag plus temp file and atomic rename). The record's wording 'symlink targets were not rechecked after resolution' corresponds to the swallowed denial described here.

classes: What is shown versus what is used
root_cause: Approval of an MCP server entry was bound to the entry once accepted rather than to its content, so later changes to the approved entry's command ran without re-approval or any warning.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only (the cursor/cursor GitHub repository holds issues and advisories, not source). GHSA lists affected below 1.2.4 and patched 1.3; other sources say 1.2.4 and below.

root_cause: The agent could create a dotfile that did not yet exist without user approval (only edits to existing dotfiles needed approval), so instructions injected through MCP-provided content could create `.cursor/mcp.json`, whose commands were then started without approval.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. GHSA lists affected up to 1.2.1 and patched 1.3.9. The create-versus-edit difference also matches the facet 'Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points'.

component: GitHub Copilot agent in Visual Studio 2022 / Visual Studio Code
root_cause: The coding agent could write workspace settings files such as `.vscode/settings.json` without asking the user, and the auto-approval setting for tool calls (`chat.tools.autoApprove`) could be turned on from workspace settings, so instructions injected through content the agent read could widen the agent's own permissions and then run commands.
notes: Question-level test only: the CVE record and MSRC list only Visual Studio 2022 17.14 (affected from 17.14.0, fixed in 17.14.12, August 2025), which is closed source, and no public fix commit is tied to the CVE. Public VS Code changes with the same effect exist but none mentions the CVE, so the link is unconfirmed: microsoft/vscode 3cdb459b3cf0afe6e12cff962a037354f3197069 and 03f37de8fb95374b10fb2abc31e92a50f0408447 scope chat.tools.autoApprove to APPLICATION_MACHINE (user settings only) from tag 1.103.0 (in src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.contribution.ts); microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat d272630a0f3a7b5c9fa3f152f85e551af0460240 adds confirmation for agent edits to .vscode/*.json (src/extension/tools/node/editFileToolUtils.tsx), first in tag v0.31.0. A re-tester who wants source can audit src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/ at vscode tag 1.102.3 and src/extension/tools/node/ at vscode-copilot-chat v0.30.3, but these are not confirmed to be the CVE's fix.

root_cause: With the embedded ASAR integrity fuse on, only the ASAR archive was validated at startup; the V8 heap startup snapshot file loaded from the application directory was never checked, so code in a modified snapshot ran inside an integrity-checked app.
notes: Main fix fdf29ce8 (parent 3770bb31a7aabd20457d73ad7610dc3b9b6d3d3d). Backports: 38-x-y 2e5a0b7220ebf955c6785cc5adb2e2b1cf77dac1 (fixed v38.0.0-beta.6), 37-x-y 23a02934510fcf951428e14573d9b2d2a3c4f28b (vulnerable v37.3.0, fixed v37.3.1), 36-x-y 3f92511cdecc39f46b0e86cce40a0c691e301c9d (fixed v36.8.1), 35-x-y 5be0be7f0418e0a388cf84ad34ee475dbda76266 (fixed v35.7.5). The fix embeds and checks a hash of the snapshot. Only apps with the embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation and onlyLoadAppFromAsar fuses on are affected. The integrity machinery also spans shell/common/asar/ and Chromium patches under patches/chromium/.

root_cause: The request-body parser was chosen by the request's content type (multipart parser only for `multipart/form-data`), but the Form, Chat Trigger and Webhook file handlers read `files` from the parsed body and copied `file.filepath` without checking that the multipart parser had produced it, so a non-multipart body could supply that structure itself.
notes: The fix commit is a private-fork security merge titled 'Merge commit from fork' (parent e45a4b1073d85d04d6455a4f18482838a7840124); it asserts `req.contentType === 'multipart/form-data'` in the three file handlers. Affected 1.65.0 up to but not including 1.121.0; first fixed tag n8n@1.121.0; last affected tag n8n@1.120.4 (no backport). In the Webhook node the new check is defence in depth, because webhook() already routes only multipart requests there. The Armis page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch.

root_cause: Deployment guides for Sitecore XP 9.0 and earlier and Active Directory 1.4 shipped a sample ASP.NET machineKey that sites used unchanged in production, so ViewState signed with that public key passed MAC validation and was deserialized into objects.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Sitecore Security Bulletin SC2025-005. Also affects multi-instance deployments with customer-managed static machine keys. For a re-test, the reviewable artifacts are the web.config machineKey handling and the deployment documentation, not product source.

root_cause: The admission webhook, which has no caller authentication, built an nginx configuration from the submitted Ingress object and ran `nginx -t` on it, so directives injected through Ingress fields were evaluated by the nginx binary inside the controller.
notes: Each branch got one squash commit 'Controller: Several security fixes.' that also fixes CVE-2025-1097, CVE-2025-1098, CVE-2025-24513 and CVE-2025-24514: release-1.12 626305229 (parent cfd4d89a5608f53c6bcb1e477818ad9d8fe70914, first fixed controller-v1.12.1, last affected controller-v1.12.0), main cfe3923b (PR #13068, first fixed controller-v1.13.0), release-1.11 e6716b13 (first fixed controller-v1.11.5, last affected controller-v1.11.4). The CVE-2025-1974 part alone is PR-branch commit 0ccf4caa 'Controller: Deactivate configuration test during validation.', which is not on any release branch by itself. The fix disables the config test in CheckIngress; it does not add webhook authentication. That controller-v1.12.0 is an ancestor of the 1.12 fix parent was inferred, not verified.

root_cause: The WSUS client web service decrypted the request's `AuthorizationCookie` with a fixed AES key and passed the plaintext to BinaryFormatter deserialization without type restrictions, treating successful decryption as proof of trust.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Only servers with the WSUS Server Role enabled are affected. Method names reported in analyses (GetCookie on the client web service) come from decompiled code.

root_cause: The `/api/v1/auth/force-reset-password` endpoint allowed anonymous access, and when the request body set `IsSysAdmin` to true it took a branch that reset the system administrator's password without verifying the old password or a reset token.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. Fixed in build 9511 (January 2026); watchTowr tracked it as WT-2026-0001 before the CVE was assigned. The method named in analyses of decompiled code is AuthenticationService.ForceResetPassword.

id: DOM-based clickjacking of password manager extensions (DEF CON 33, 2025, no CVE)
component: Password manager browser extensions (open-source reference instance: Bitwarden browser extension)
classes: What is shown versus what is used
root_cause: The autofill inline menu was injected as ordinary page DOM, and its checks for being obscured (last-child position and the element at its center point) ignored opacity inherited from the host page's `html`/`body` and page content in the browser top layer, so the host page could make the menu transparent or cover it while clicks still reached it.
notes: Multi-vendor sample with no CVE (CERT/CC VU#516608 lists none); Bitwarden is used as the open-source reference instance, and the other vendors are question-level only. Bitwarden fix in three steps: e7059b7 (parent f157d8c3f5402c4efcc0c6718aa3a9943f12d0c7, first in browser-v2025.8.0) closes the menu when html or body opacity is low; 4af4a86 (first in browser-v2025.8.1) adds top-layer checks; f921012 (parent = browser-v2025.8.1) renders the menu in the top layer, first fixed tag browser-v2025.8.2. vulnerable_ref is the fully unmitigated code; the researcher lists browser-v2025.8.1 as still affected. Per the researcher's post (updated January 2026), 1Password and LastPass remained affected and about ten other vendors shipped fixes. KeePassXC-Browser 1.9.11 includes PR #2733 'Check overlays before fill' (commit 20f1a99356e0198924c50c69421e67cab05a008a), which the researcher does not map to his finding.
